proposals.before: He submitted writings to the court, passed the Secretariat examination, rose to Right Reminder, served twice as Attendant of Leftness in charge of imperial-clan memorials, and then drafted edicts as Director of the Ministry of Rites Office.
proposals.after: He submitted writings to the court, passed the Secretariat examination, rose to Right Reminder, was transferred to Court Diarist in charge of imperial-clan memorials, and then drafted edicts as Director of Merit Evaluation in the Ministry of Rites.
proposals.reason: 起居郎 is Court Diarist/Imperial Diarist, not 'Attendant of Leftness'; 考功郎中 is Director of Merit Evaluation.

proposals.before: He presented writings at the court, passed the Secretariat examination, was promoted to Right Reminder, transferred twice to Attendant of Leftness, managed imperial-clan memorials, and as Director of the Ministry of Rites Office drafted edicts.
proposals.after: He presented writings at the court, passed the Secretariat examination, was promoted to Right Reminder, transferred to Court Diarist, managed imperial-clan memorials, and as Director of Merit Evaluation drafted edicts.
proposals.reason: Same office mistranslation of 起居郎 as 'Attendant of Leftness'.

proposals.before: When the emperor went hunting in Sword South, he was appointed Secretariat Drafter.

proposals.reason: 扈狩劍南 refers to escorting the imperial progress/flight to Jiannan, not a hunt ('Sword South').

proposals.before: The emperor was enraged and demoted Kui to Long Chief of Yuan Prefecture.

proposals.before: The emperor was angry and demoted Kui to Long Chief of Yuan Prefecture.

proposals.before: In the Baoying period they were constructing the Taizong and Jianling mausoleums with broad expenditures; also Tibet raided the border; scholars throughout recommended famine; Jing in plain dress submitted a memorial requesting reduction of rites and thrift—the scholarly world sighed in admiration.
proposals.after: In the Baoying period they were constructing the Tai and Jian mausoleums with broad expenditures; also Tibet raided the border; famine spread across the realm; Jing in plain dress submitted a memorial requesting reduction of rites and thrift—the scholarly world sighed in admiration.
proposals.reason: 天下薦饑 means widespread famine, not 'scholars throughout recommended famine'.

proposals.before: He was tested as assistant magistrate of Jiangxia, served in several commissioner offices, and advanced to Queller of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.after: He was tested as assistant magistrate of Jiangxia, served in several commissioner offices, and advanced to Cadet of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.reason: 太子舍人 is a cadet/retainer of the heir apparent, not 'Queller'.

proposals.before: He was tested as Assistant Magistrate of Jiangxia, assisted various commissioner offices, and advanced to Queller of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.after: He was tested as Assistant Magistrate of Jiangxia, assisted various commissioner offices, and advanced to Cadet of the Heir Apparent.

proposals.before: Huang hated the Vice Director of the Directorate Zhang Can; Gun hated the Heir Apparent's Junior Administrator Zhao Ji. Both men received reduced stipends.
proposals.after: Huang hated Zhang Can, Vice Director of the Directorate; Gun hated Zhao Ji, the Heir Apparent's Junior Administrator. Both men received reduced stipends.
proposals.reason: English fuses office and name as 'Directorate Zhang Can'; reorder so Zhang Can is clearly the person.

proposals.before: When he became chief minister he promoted Jing from Director of the Court of Judicial Review to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat. Gen had just been demoted to Vice Prefect of Quzhou, and [Jing] brought him in as Prefect of Jizhou—people regarded this as worthy.
proposals.after: When he became chief minister he promoted Cui Jing from Director of the Court of Judicial Review to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat. Gen had just been demoted to Vice Prefect of Quzhou, and [Zhao Jing] brought him in as Prefect of Jizhou—people regarded this as worthy.
proposals.reason: Bare 'Jing' for 儆 collides with Zhao Jing (憬) in the same sentence; the first referent is Cui Jing and the later silent subject is Zhao Jing.

proposals.before: After the capital was restored he was recalled. When he reached Lantian he learned that his uncle Yuan Xiu had joined the rebels, and he submitted a memorial asking to be punished.
proposals.after: After the capital was restored he was recalled. When he reached Lantian, taking his maternal uncle Yuan Xiu to have joined the rebels in treason, he submitted a memorial asking to be punished.
proposals.reason: Chinese 自以 marks his own judgment that his maternal uncle had joined the rebels, not newly learned information.

proposals.before: Zao feared this. He first feigned illness to resign and was then dismissed to Right Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's household; Xiu was demoted to Revenue Officer of Lei Prefecture.
proposals.after: Zao feared this. He first pleaded illness to resign and was then dismissed to Right Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's household; Xiu was demoted to Revenue Officer of Lei Prefecture.
proposals.reason: 托疾 here matches the idiomatic 'pleaded illness'; 'feigned' asserts deceit the Chinese does not require.

proposals.before: San Cheng Commissioner Ma Sui recruited him as administrative aide.

proposals.before: He fled to Fengtian and was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

proposals.before: Whenever Mai had merit mourning or lesser mourning he always accommodated himself to the proper garments, yet showed extra feeling.
proposals.after: Whenever Mai observed mourning of the gong grade or the si grade, he always accommodated himself to the proper garments, yet showed extra feeling.
proposals.reason: 功、緦喪 denotes mourning grades (功喪 and 緦喪), not merit mourning; the literal misreads 功 as merit.

proposals.before: When his cousin brother Yin returned from mourning to Luoyang and passed the capital, Mai memorialized to go weep for him and mourned to the full.

proposals.reason: Cousin brother is unnatural English for 從父弟; passed the capital omits the through-sense of 過都.
